title: Perpetual funding carry (long spot / short perpetual)
economic_hypothesis: Perpetual futures have no expiry, so the venue pays a funding rate to keep the contract tethered to spot. When funding is positive and persistent, holding spot against a short perpetual harvests that payment while staying delta-neutral: the carry is a structural transfer from leveraged longs to liquidity providers.
market: crypto spot and perpetual futures (two venues in the classic form)
timeframe: 8-hour funding cycles, positions held for weeks
entry_rules: PARTIAL: the source family describes the delta-neutral construction (long spot, short perp) and conditions on the sign/persistence of funding; exact thresholds are not fixed at the level read.
risk_rules: UNKNOWN as a source rule; liquidation risk on the short leg is the central practical hazard.
parameters: Funding thresholds and rebalancing bands are not stated at the level read.
claimed_period: three years for S-19; UNKNOWN for S-14/S-15
claimed_metrics: S-14: Sharpe 3.35 for the Bitcoin carry strategy even under high retail trading costs. S-19: 16.0% annualised, Sharpe 6.1 on tick data. S-15: a high Sharpe ratio for the crypto carry trade. S-20: funding is now benchmarked by an index provider.
transaction_cost_model: S-14 explicitly models high retail costs; others are unclear.
required_data: spot and perpetual prices plus funding history (public)
external_results: This is the best-evidenced family in the registry: a maintained academic working paper with a high-cost scenario, plus multiple independent papers agreeing.
counter_evidence: Instrument fit: the project runtime excludes derivatives by contract, and this strategy cannot exist without a perpetual short on margin.

Capital fit: a delta-neutral position across two venues needs collateral on both; the reference capital is 200 USDT and the project's own prior review of a comparable institutional line put minimum viable capital at 25M-50M USD.
Crowding: an index provider now publishes a benchmark funding rate (S-20), which is what a capacity-limited carry looks like once institutions are in it.
The project has already measured that its own carry-adjacent line is below cost (closed carry line in WHERE_WE_ARE.md: 'carry predictable but below cost').
ambiguities: No statement of what part of the funding survives fees, borrow and rebalancing at small size.
Venue/counterparty risk is not modelled by any source.
replication_difficulty: LOW methodologically, IMPOSSIBLE within the current runtime contract.
selection_note: Recorded as the highest-scoring rejection: the evidence is strong, but the line requires instruments and collateral the project does not run and cannot fund. It is not a candidate for replication; it is a candidate for a different business.
